name: Kocatepe Mosque
features: Neo-classical Ottoman design inspired by the Selimiye Mosque, with four 88 m minarets.
note: Article lead image is Free Art License so not used; only qualifying file in category, title 'Ankara camii' - confirm it is the exterior.

name: Çanakkale Martyrs' Memorial
by: Doğan Erginbaş, İsmail Utkular, Ertuğrul Barla
features: Four 7.5 m square columns carry a 25 by 25 m concrete slab.
note: Lead image of en.wikipedia article (description 'Gallipoli Peninsula Historical Site'). Year = opening (main structure finished 1958).

name: Ankara Ethnography Museum
features: Designed by Arif Hikmet Koyunoğlu and built between 1925 and 1928.
note: no free photo. No free photo found directly in the category (files are in per-year subcategories; not checked). Article gives no features beyond architect and dates; features line and concepts are thin.

name: Ankara Palas
features: Symmetrical two-storey building with a domed central entrance flanked by twin towers.
note: Only >=1200px file in category; description is just the title, so identity from category. Lead image is 800px.

name: Istanbul Archaeology Museums
features: Facade inspired by the Alexander Sarcophagus and Sarcophagus of the Mourning Women.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article.

name: Haydarpaşa Terminal
features: Neo-classical station on land reclaimed from the sea, resting on 1,100 wooden piles.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (description 'Haydarpaşa Train Station, 2014').

name: Sirkeci Terminal
features: Orientalist terminal building with gas lighting and heating from large tile stoves.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (descriptions name Sirkeci).

name: Dolmabahçe Palace
by: Garabet Balyan, Nigoğayos Balyan, Evanis Kalfa
features: Eclectic Baroque, Rococo and Neoclassical design with a European two-wing plan seen from the Bosphorus.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'Dolmabahçe Palace seen from Bosphorus').

name: Istanbul Airport
by: Grimshaw Architects, Nordic Office of Architecture, Haptic Architects
features: Control tower shaped like a tulip; first-stage terminal covers about 1.44 million square metres.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'main building'). Judgement call whether it counts as an ordinary type.

name: Şehzade Mosque
features: Square plan under a central dome flanked by four half-domes; richly carved twin minarets.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article.

name: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
features: Iznik tiles cover almost every vertical surface; plan is an octagon inscribed in a rectangle.
note: Exterior view from Karaköy ferry per category listing; file name reconstructed from API output, verify exact name. Lead image is only 480x640.

name: Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, Edirnekapı
features: A cube topped by a half-sphere, with so many windows it is one of Sinan's lightest interiors.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (descriptions 'Whole view of the mosque' / 'Mosque exterior').

name: Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital
features: Main north portal celebrated for its dense high-relief stone carving.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (WLM Turkey upload). Lead image is only 1024px.

name: Hagia Sophia
by: Isidore of Miletus, Anthemius of Tralles
features: One of the first buildings with a fully pendentive dome, about 33 m across after rebuilding.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article.

name: Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque)
features: Central dome surrounded by four semi-domes, each flanked by three smaller ones; six minarets.

photos.file: File:Istanbul's Blue Mosque from the courtyard.jpg

note: file in the building's own Commons category (descriptions 'Blue Mosque'). Article lead image not available via pageimages.

name: Green Mosque, Bursa
features: Cube-shaped two-storey building on an inverted T plan with a white marble fountain under the central dome.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'Green Mosque of Bursa'). Year: inscription says completed Dec 1419/Jan 1420; infobox says 1424.

name: Grand Mosque of Bursa
features: Interior covered by twenty domes in four rows of five on twelve columns, with a central fountain.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (skyline view of the mosque).

name: Çamlıca Mosque
features: Large box attached to a colonnaded courtyard, with a squat central dome and six minarets.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'Çamlıca Republic Mosque as seen from the Bosporus').

name: Troy Museum
features: Four-storey cube clad in rust-coloured weathering steel, as tall as the excavation is deep.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (description names the weathering-steel cube exterior). Lead image is a logo.

name: Beylerbeyi Palace
features: Simpler than Dolmabahçe; two bathing pavilions are best seen from the Bosphorus.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article.

name: Atakule
features: Tower with a revolving restaurant that turns 360 degrees in one hour.
note: Lead image is Free Art License so not used; chosen from category (description 'Tower designed by architect Ragıp Buluç; built 1987–1989').

name: TCDD General Headquarters Building
features: Wide steps to the main entrance; colonnade marble from Bilecik and Hereke matches the stone.
note: no free photo. Lead image is Free Art License, not allowed; no other photo checked. Movement label is a judgement (article calls the style grandiose, linked to fascist architecture).

name: Gök Medrese, Sivas
features: Two 25 m minarets flank the portal; sky-blue tiles give the 'Blue Madrasah' its name.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'Gök Medrese').

name: Istanbul University Faculty of Arts and Sciences Building
by: Sedad Hakkı Eldem, Emin Halid Onat
features: Stone-faced arcades and colonnades; second national era of Turkish architecture, Paul Bonatz advising.
note: no free photo. No lead image; Commons category search found nothing. Not photo-checked further.

name: Istanbul Grand Post Office
features: Atrium topped by orange and blue glass; 16th-century classical Ottoman ornament throughout.
note: file in the building's own Commons category (descriptions 'Exterior of the Grand Post Office Building'). Article lead image is a general Istanbul view, not used.

name: Istanbul Lütfi Kırdar Convention and Exhibition Center
by: Paolo Vietti-Violi, Şinasi Şahingiray, Fazıl Aysu
features: Opened 1949 as the country's only indoor sports and exhibition hall; extended underground in 2009.

photos.file: File:Lütfi Kırdar Convention and Exhibition Center.JPG

note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description 'Main building'). Year = opening; movement is a judgement.

name: SantralIstanbul
by: İhsan Bilgin, Nevzat Sayın, Emre Arolat, Han Tümertekin
features: Neutral new buildings with aluminium-mesh facades beside the historic power station.
note: file in the building's own Commons category ('SantralIstanbul exterior'). Wikipedia URL read via API-style title; 'by' lists coordinating and component architects named in the article. Year = opening 2007.

name: Caferağa Medrese
features: Gate leads to an inner courtyard around which the learning rooms stand.
note: lead image of the en.wikipedia article (description names Caferağa Medresseh built by Sinan).

name: Vahdat Hall (Rudaki Hall)
features: Main stage on three levels; proscenium curtain with a phoenix rising from the ashes motif.
note: no free photo: category and lead image show only concerts/interiors, nothing of the exterior

name: Milad Tower
features: Octagonal base tied to traditional Iranian architecture; steel head of 12 floors with a revolving restaurant.
note: Photo 1 found by Commons search, description 'Milad Tower'; photo 2 in own category (800x1253 only). Wikipedia lead image is a non-Commons en file (456x800), not used. Opened Oct 2008; 2007 = construction finished.

name: Tomb of Ferdowsi
features: Achaemenid-style tomb: a cubical upper structure with four pillars around it, on a wide base.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Article says Lurzadeh designed it originally, present design credited mainly to Taherzadeh; 1934 = year permanent tomb was erected. Hooshang Seyhoun's later design is not covered in the part I read.

name: Tomb of Saadi
features: Eight brown stone pillars at the front; octagonal interior with marble walls and a blue arch.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Photo 2 is from the building's own category, description 'Aramgah-e Sa'di'.

name: National Museum of Iran (Iran Bastan Museum)
features: Brick building of about 11,000 sq m with a design influenced by Sassanid vaults, notably Taq Kasra.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Commons description names the museum. Opened 1937.

name: Nasir al-Mulk Mosque
features: Extensive stained glass in the facade; 'Panj Kase' (five concaved) design.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Commons description names the mosque. Article calls it Nasir al-Mulk Mosque (title Nasir-ol-Molk Mosque).

name: Golestan Palace
features: Mirror-work Brilliant Hall and a Windcatcher Mansion with traditional windcatchers.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Article: palace rebuilt to its current form in 1865 by Mimar Navai; Edifice of the Sun begun 1865, finished two years later; Mirror Hall by Sanie ol Molk. Complex has no single completion year.

name: University of Baghdad (Jadriyah campus)
features: Gropius master plan for a new campus with engineering and liberal arts schools for 6,000 students.
note: CHECK FIRST: category is the whole university and has no description naming Gropius's buildings; photo 1 has no description, photo 2 is the university tower from the Karkh side. Not confirmed these show Gropius-era buildings. Article says 'Gropius, Louis McMillen and Robert McMillah', built 1959-60 (Gropius template: 1957-1960).

name: Central Bank of Iraq
features: Cubical reinforced-concrete building clad in marble, few outer openings, organised around an inner courtyard.
note: no free photo: category's only photo (1024x768, CC BY 2.0) shows it as a distant backdrop to the Mustansiriya Madrasa

name: Republican Palace, Baghdad
features: Modernist palace first designed as a central domed section with two wings; fountain in front part of original design.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Year conflict in article: infobox 1958, lead 'early 1960s'. Later additions under Saddam Hussein, so photo may show the expanded building.

name: Abboud Building (Al-Dhakir)
features: Unusual cylindrical form and bright white colour, a modernist nod to its surroundings and the past.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Only 715x933 (below 1200); no larger free file found by search. Commons description 'Al-Dhakir Building, Abboud Building'.

name: Mausoleum of Omar Khayyam
features: White marble monument with a star-shaped opening to the sky and calligraphic tiles of Khayyam's poems.
note: Identity: Wikipedia article lead image (pageimages API) and Commons description; not viewed. Commons description is only a wiki link; identity rests on the article lead.
